extracted.intended_audience: Authors submitting manuscripts to Archive for Mathematical Logic (researchers in mathematical logic)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting research and non-research manuscripts to the journal Archive for Mathematical Logic, covering formatting, ethical requirements, data and figure specifications, authorship, and post-acceptance procedures. Intended to ensure submissions meet Springer Nature and journal policies for peer review and publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and simultaneous submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a manuscript implies that the work described has not been published before and is not under consideration for publication anywhere else.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The work must be original; submission implies publication has been approved by all co-authors and the responsible authorities at the institute. Violation may lead to rejection and legal issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions for previously published material
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors wishing to include figures, tables, or text passages already published elsewhere are required to obtain permission from the copyright owner(s) for both print and online formats and include evidence of such permission when submitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material received without permission evidence will be assumed to originate from the authors. Some publishers may not grant electronic rights for free; Springer will not refund permission costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of editable source files
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide all relevant editable source files at every submission and revision; failing to submit a complete set of editable source files will result in the article not being considered for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscript text should be submitted in common word processing formats such as .docx or LaTeX; for LaTeX submissions include all style files and figures and a PDF of compiled output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting required declarations at submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Author Contribution information and Competing Interest information must be provided at submission via the submission interface; only information submitted via the interface will be used in the final published version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial board members who are authors must declare this in the Competing Interest section of the interface. See relevant guideline sections for mandatory statements and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title page content
rubrics_metrics.description: Title page must contain: concise informative title; author names; affiliations (institution, department, city, state, country); clear indication and active e-mail of corresponding author; ORCID if available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If address info is provided it will be published. Unaffiliated authors: only city and country of residence captured. Include author acknowledgments/funding on title page in separate section.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM (AI) authorship and use policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Large Language Models (LLMs) do not satisfy authorship criteria and cannot be listed as authors. Use of LLMs must be documented in Methods (or suitable alternative) when used; AI-assisted copy editing does not need declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI-assisted copy editing defined as improvements to human-generated text for readability/style/grammar that do not include generative editorial work or autonomous content creation. Human accountability for final text is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract length and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an abstract of 150 to 250 words that should not contain undefined abbreviations or unspecified references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For clinical trials include trial registration number and date (prospective or 'retrospectively registered' as applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Keywords for indexing
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide 4 to 6 keywords which can be used for indexing purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statements and Declarations inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must include a 'Statements and Declarations' section containing Competing Interests and other relevant declarations; submissions lacking relevant declarations will be returned as incomplete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See sections on Competing Interests and Funding for how to complete; revise sample wording to suit your situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematics Subject Classification (MSC) codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an appropriate number of MSC codes to categorize the manuscript for reviewing databases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use www.ams.org/msc for MSC codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text formatting and LaTeX recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts should be submitted in LaTeX; authors are encouraged to use the Springer Nature LaTeX template. Submission should include original source (style files and figures) and a PDF of compiled output. Word files are also accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all relevant editable source files are provided at each submission and revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headings system
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the decimal system of headings with no more than three levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Abbreviations should be defined at first mention and used consistently thereafter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnotes rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Footnotes can provide additional information including citation of a reference included in the reference list but should not consist solely of a reference citation nor include bibliographic details; do not include figures or tables in footnotes; use footnotes instead of endnotes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnotes to text numbered consecutively; footnotes to tables indicated by superscript lower-case letters (or asterisks for statistical data). No reference symbols for footnotes to title or authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgments placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledgments of people, grants, funds, etc. should be placed in a separate section on the title page; funding organization names should be written in full.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific notation style
rubrics_metrics.description: Use standard mathematical notation: italic for single letters denoting variables/constants; roman/upright for numerals, operators, and commonly defined functions (e.g., cos, det, e, exp, lim, log, max); bold for vectors, tensors, and matrices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation style and reference list
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference citations in text should be identified by numbers in square brackets; the reference list should include only works cited in the text and published or accepted for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal communications and unpublished works should only be mentioned in the text. Entries must be numbered consecutively. If available, always include DOIs as full DOI links in the reference list. Use standard journal name abbreviations per ISSN LTWA; when unsure, use full journal title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table numbering and captions
rubrics_metrics.description: All tables must be numbered using Arabic numerals and cited in text in consecutive numerical order; each table must have a caption explaining its components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify any previously published material in the table by giving the original source as a reference at the end of the table caption. Use footnotes to tables indicated by superscript lower-case letters (or asterisks for stats) beneath the table body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic figure submission and formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply all figures electronically; indicate which graphics program created the artwork. Preferred formats: EPS for vector graphics, TIFF for halftones; MSOffice files also acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name figure files with 'Fig' and figure number, e.g., Fig1.eps. Vector graphics containing fonts must have fonts embedded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line art technical specs
rubrics_metrics.description: Line art: black and white graphics with no shading; avoid faint lines/lettering and ensure legible at final size. All lines should be at least 0.1 mm (0.3 pt) wide. Scanned line drawings/bitmap line drawings should have minimum resolution 1200 dpi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vector graphics with fonts must have fonts embedded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Halftone art technical specs
rubrics_metrics.description: Halftone art (photographs, drawings with fine shading) should have a minimum resolution of 300 dpi; indicate magnification with scale bars if used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination artwork resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Combination art (halftone + line art) should have a minimum resolution of 600 dpi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include halftones containing line drawing, extensive lettering, color diagrams, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color art guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Color art is free of charge for online publication. If print will be black and white, ensure main information remains visible without color; avoid referring to color in captions if print will be black and white. Color illustrations should be submitted as RGB (8 bits per channel).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check xerographic copies to ensure distinguishability when converted to black and white.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure lettering and fonts
rubrics_metrics.description: Use sans serif fonts (Helvetica or Arial) for figure lettering; keep lettering consistently sized throughout final-sized artwork (about 2–3 mm / 8–12 pt); minimize variance of type size within an illustration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid effects such as shading, outline letters; do not include titles or captions within illustrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure numbering and part labels
rubrics_metrics.description: Number all figures using Arabic numerals and cite them in text in consecutive order; denote figure parts by lowercase letters (a, b, c, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an appendix contains figures, continue the main text numbering (do not use A1, A2), but figures in online appendices (SI) should be numbered separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure captions formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Each figure must have a concise caption describing accurately what the figure depicts; include captions in the main text file, not in figure files. Captions begin with the term 'Fig.' in bold followed by the figure number in bold; no punctuation after the number or at end of caption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify all elements found in the figure in the caption and cite previously published material by reference at end of caption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure placement and sizing
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit figures within the body of the text; if file size causes upload problems, large figures may be submitted separately. Size figures to fit column width with specified width/height limits depending on journal size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For large-sized journals: 84 mm (double-column) or 174 mm (single-column) wide and not higher than 234 mm. For small-sized journals: 119 mm wide and not higher than 195 mm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure accessibility requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure figures are accessible: provide descriptive captions for use with text-to-speech or Braille, use patterns in addition to/instead of colors to convey information, and ensure figure lettering has a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generative AI images policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should check Springer’s policy on generative AI images and make sure work adheres to the principles described therein.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary Information formats and submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic multimedia files and other supplementary files (animations, movies, audio, etc.) are accepted for online publication alongside an article; supply all supplementary material in standard file formats and include article title, journal name, author names, affiliation and corresponding author e-mail inside each file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Larger files may have long download times—consider user experience. Number and name files consecutively (e.g., ESM_3.mpg). Text/presentations: PDF format. Spreadsheets: .csv or .xlsx. Specialized formats (.pdb, .wrl, .nb, .tex) can be supplied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary video technical specs
rubrics_metrics.description: Video/animations: aspect ratio 16:9 or 4:3; maximum file size 2 GB; minimum duration 1 sec; supported formats include avi, wmv, mp4, mov, m2p, mp2, mpg, mpeg, flv, mxf, mts, m4v, 3gp.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary Information numbering and citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary files must be specifically mentioned in the main text as citations similar to figures and tables and referred to as 'Online Resource X'; name files consecutively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise caption for each supplementary material. Supplementary figures in SI should be numbered separately from main text figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing and publication of supplementary files
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary Information will be published as received from the author without conversion, editing, or reformatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility for supplementary files
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure SI is accessible: manuscript should contain descriptive captions for each supplementary material; video files should not contain flashing more than three times per second to avoid seizure risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of editing services
rubrics_metrics.description: Using professional author services (English language editing, developmental comments, formatting, figure preparation, translation) is optional and not a requirement for publication nor does it guarantee acceptance. A free Grammar Check tool is available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of services does not imply editorial favor. Services are offered in multiple languages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical responsibilities and COPE adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal follows COPE guidelines and expects authors to refrain from misrepresenting research results and to uphold integrity of the scientific record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidelines include: no simultaneous submissions, originality, avoid salami-slicing, present results honestly (no fabrication/falsification/inappropriate data manipulation), adhere to discipline-specific data rules, avoid plagiarism, secure permissions for software/questionnaires, cite appropriate literature, avoid untrue statements about entities, identify dual-use research risks. Journal may use software to screen plagiarism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of fundamental errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are obliged to correct mistakes once they discover significant errors or inaccuracies in their published article; contact the journal to explain impact and decide on correction or retraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retraction retains article on platform with 'retracted' watermark and explanatory note. Institution may be informed; possible measures include erratum, expression of concern, or retraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggesting and excluding reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may suggest suitable reviewers and/or request exclusion of certain individuals when submitting; suggested reviewers must be independent and not connected to the work in any way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend a mix of reviewers from different countries/institutions. Provide institutional email for each suggested reviewer or other verification (personal homepage, publication record, researcher ID). Journal may not use suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship consent prior to submission
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors are assumed to have agreed with the content and given explicit consent to submit and to have obtained consent from responsible authorities at the institute before submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publisher does not prescribe exact contributions that warrant authorship but recommends following field-specific guidelines or the provided criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship contribution criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended authorship criteria: (1) substantial contributions to conception/design, or acquisition/analysis/interpretation of data, or creation of new software; (2) drafting or critical revision for important intellectual content; (3) approval of version to be published; (4) agreement to be accountable for all aspects of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on/adapted from ICMJE and other authorship guidance. Use contribution statements to specify each author's role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosures and declarations required
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must include information regarding sources of funding, financial or non-financial interests, ethics committee approvals for human/animal research, informed consent for human participants, and animal welfare statements if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision to include specific information depends on journal scope and article scope. Corresponding author should collect documentation and provide upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data transparency and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should ensure all data, materials, software, or custom code that support published claims are available and comply with field standards; journals may have specific data-sharing policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are encouraged to deposit supporting data in publicly available repositories and to include Data Availability Statements. For sensitive data describe access conditions and participant consent; guidance available for sensitive data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corresponding author responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: One author is assigned as Corresponding Author acting on behalf of all co-authors and ensuring questions about accuracy/integrity are addressed; responsible for ensuring all authors approved manuscript, managing communication with journal, providing transparency on reuse of material, and assembling disclosures/declarations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Managing communication may be delegated to a Contact/Submitting Author but Corresponding Author must be clearly indicated. Make sure disclosures and data statements from all authors are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author contribution statements and CRediT taxonomy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are recommended to include contribution statements specifying each author's contributions; examples include free-text statements or use of the CRediT taxonomy (Conceptualization, Methodology, Formal analysis, Writing - original draft, Writing - review & editing, Funding acquisition, Resources, Supervision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For review articles or thesis-based articles provide statements appropriate to the format (e.g., who had idea, who performed literature search, who drafted/revised).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliation and author name rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary affiliation should be the institution where majority of work was done; current address may be added if moved. Author names will be published exactly as they appear on accepted submission; ensure correct spelling and current addresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses will not be updated after publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes to authorship policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are strongly advised to ensure correct author group, corresponding author, and order at submission. Changes (adding/deleting authors or changing order) are not accepted after acceptance; changes at revision stage are generally not permitted but may be warranted with explanation and at Editor-in-Chief discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Names will be published exactly as on accepted submission. Approval of changes during revision is discretionary; different journals may have individual policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCID recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are recommended to use ORCID IDs when submitting or acquire an ORCID via submission process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deceased or incapacitated authors guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: If a co-author dies or is incapacitated and co-authors wish to include them, obtain approval from a legal representative (could be a direct relative).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship disputes handling
rubrics_metrics.description: The Journal will not adjudicate authorship disputes during peer review or after acceptance; authors should resolve disputes themselves. If unable, the Journal may withdraw a manuscript or raise the issue with authors' institution(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of journal communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should treat all communication with the Journal as confidential, including correspondence with Editors and reviewers' reports, unless explicit consent is given to share information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance statements and editorial rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should include appropriate 'Compliance with Ethical Standards' statements (conflicts of interest, research involving humans/animals, informed consent) and be prepared to provide documentation; Editors reserve the right to reject manuscripts that do not comply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponding author should be prepared to collect and send documentation during peer review or after publication if requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing interests disclosure specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must disclose interests directly or indirectly related to the work. Interests within the last 3 years of beginning the work should be reported; interests outside 3 years must be disclosed if they could be perceived as influencing the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose funding, employment, financial interests (stocks, consultancies, patents), and non-financial interests (editorial positions, advisory roles, mentoring). Provide examples of wording and use a 'Declarations' section before references. Practical guideline: disclose any undeclared financial interest that could embarrass the author if publicly known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of declarations and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize funding, competing interests, ethics approval, consent, data/material/code availability and authors' contributions in a 'Declarations' section placed before the reference list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all authors have same/no conflicts, a blanket statement is sufficient. Examples of statements for funded, unfunded, and interests-to-declare are provided in the guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: After acceptance procedures and proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: After acceptance the article goes to Production for typesetting; authors will receive emails to confirm affiliation, choose publishing model, arrange rights and payment, and a link to proofs once typesetting is complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs are for checking typesetting/conversion errors and completeness; substantial changes (new results, corrected values, title, authorship) are not allowed without Editor approval. After online publication, further changes require an Erratum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article publishing agreement and copyright
rubrics_metrics.description: Depending on journal ownership/policy, authors will either grant Publisher an exclusive licence or transfer copyright. Open Choice retains copyright with author and publishes under a Creative Commons license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details of OA licenses are in the journal's 'How to publish with us' guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offprints and color illustration charges after acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Offprints can be ordered by corresponding author. Online color illustrations are free; for color in print authors may be expected to contribute toward extra costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Choice (open access) option
rubrics_metrics.description: Open Choice allows authors to publish open access in many Springer Nature journals; APCs vary by journal and benefits include increased access and higher visibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open Choice articles use Creative Commons licences; see funding/support pages for APC info and finding funding for OA charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research data policy and mandatory Data Availability Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal follows Springer Nature research data policy. All original research must include a Data Availability Statement explaining how to access data supporting results, including links/citations to publicly archived datasets analysed or generated during the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If public sharing is not possible (privacy concerns), describe access conditions and reuse conditions; obtain participant consent. Authors are encouraged to consider minimal dataset necessary to interpret/replicate findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data repositories and recommended practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are strongly encouraged to deposit supporting data in publicly available repositories, preferably discipline-specific ones where available. For some data types submission to specific public repositories is mandatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journal encourages open licences for research data but does not enforce particular repository licences. Ensure rights to share deposited data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data citation format
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should cite any publicly available data on which conclusions rely using a persistent identifier (DOI) and include data citations in the reference list using DataCite minimum information (Dataset Creator, Dataset Title, Publisher [repository], Publication Year, Identifier).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See journal's further guidance on citing datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymisation of data for double-anonymous review
rubrics_metrics.description: If using double-anonymous peer review and providing reviewers access to data, authorship in the data should also be anonymised; repositories exist to mask authorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research Data Helpdesk and FAQ can assist with anonymisation and repository selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for research data policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors who need help understanding data-sharing policy, finding a suitable repository, or organising and sharing research data can consult the Research Data Helpdesk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the FAQ page for more information on Springer Nature's research data policy.
